sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Expand: (a) WWW (b) B2B (c) B2C (d) C2C.
questions.answer: (a) World Wide Web. (b) Business to Business. (c) Business to Consumer. (d) Consumer to Consumer.

questions.q: Identify in e-banking: (a) a card that allows spending up to the balance in the account; (b) a machine to withdraw money at convenience; (c) a system giving banking facility over the telephone; (d) accessing the account anytime, anywhere.
questions.answer: (a) Debit card. (b) ATM. (c) Telebanking. (d) Internet banking.

questions.q: Arrange the stages of an online transaction: order, delivery, payment, search, after-sales service.
questions.answer: Search; order; payment; delivery; after-sales service.

questions.q: Name any two e-commerce businesses.
questions.answer: Amazon and Flipkart (also eBay, Myntra, BigBasket).

questions.q: Mention the various ways of making payment in online transactions.
questions.answer: Cash on delivery, cheque, net banking, credit or debit card and digital cash.

questions.q: Name the security measure: (a) conversion of data into a code, (b) used to authenticate the sender and check integrity.
questions.answer: (a) Encryption. (b) Digital signature.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The ______ is an online record of items picked while browsing. (b) ______ means the interaction among departments within the firm.
questions.answer: (a) virtual shopping cart. (b) Intra-B commerce.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) A credit card holder can spend beyond the credit limit. (ii) E-Post helps rural people use e-mail facilities.
questions.answer: (i) False. (ii) True.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Give any two benefits of e-commerce.
questions.answer: Wider accessibility to national and global customers and savings in cost leading to lower prices (also convenience and time saving).

questions.q: What is e-Post?
questions.answer: A service in which printed or handwritten messages are sent as e-mail and printed, enveloped and delivered by the post office at the destination.

questions.q: State any two limitations of e-commerce.
questions.answer: It lacks personal touch and customers cannot see or try goods before buying.

questions.q: What is meant by intra-B commerce?
questions.answer: The interaction and dealings among departments and persons within the firm using the Internet.

questions.q: Mention one benefit of an ATM for bank customers.
questions.answer: Withdrawal or deposit of money at any time and a check of balance and mini statement without visiting the bank.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three forms of e-commerce.
questions.answer: B2B (between firms), B2C (between firms and consumers) and C2C (between consumers); C2B is the reverse of B2C.

questions.q: Explain the benefits of e-commerce (any three).
questions.answer: Wider accessibility, shorter transaction time, and cost saving with low prices (also improved service).

questions.q: Explain any three limitations of e-commerce.
questions.answer: Lack of personal touch, delivery delays and privacy and security risks.

questions.q: Explain any three precautions for security in online transactions.
questions.answer: Use passwords, encrypt data and use digital signatures (also trusted third parties and authentication).

questions.q: Distinguish between a debit card and a credit card.
questions.answer: Debit card spends up to the balance in the account; credit card allows purchases up to a credit limit with payment by a due date, interest being charged on delay.

questions.q: Explain any three e-business risks.
questions.answer: Default on order or delivery, data theft through virus or hacking and loss of privacy or intellectual property.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the stages in online transactions.
questions.answer: Search for a vendor, order through registration and shopping cart, payment, delivery and after-sales service.

questions.q: What options are available for securing online transactions? Explain.
questions.answer: Passwords, authentication, encryption, digital signatures and trusted third parties, though stolen cards and fraudulent sites need vigilance.

questions.q: Explain the applications of e-commerce.
questions.answer: E-banking, e-ticketing, e-advertising, e-trading at stock exchanges, computerised mail and e-Post, and online education.

questions.q: Explain the payment mechanisms of online transactions.
questions.answer: Cash on delivery, cheque, net banking, credit or debit card and digital cash.

questions.q: Explain the resources required for successful e-business implementation.
questions.answer: A website, trained workforce, adequate computers, effective telecommunication and a payment mechanism.
